description: We are a team of four passionate girls participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge, taking on the Martian map challenge. Our objective is to create user-friendly map of Mars that makes exploring the Red Planet more accessible and engaging. By combining our technical skills and passion for space exploration, we aim to visualize Martian geography, highlight key landmarks, and contribute to the science.
summary:
Mars remains largely unexplored, with large regions holding geological mysteries that could completely change our understanding of the planet's history. Although NASA has collected extensive data through satellites, rovers, and scientific instruments, much of this information is still spread across different datasets.
Astral Atlas aims to bridge this gap by using existing NASA observations into an interactive predictive mapping system designed to support future Martian exploration safely.
Focusing on Jezero Crater, Astral Atlas combines geological, mineralogical, topographic, and environmental data to find potentially significant features in areas with limited direct observations. By analysing relationships between existing measurements, the system aims to predict unexplored geological characteristics, highlight uncertainty, and identify locations with high scientific potential. 
Beyond mapping, Astral Atlas explores how terrain elevation, atmospheric conditions, and environmental hazards can inform astronaut route planning by predicting the safest and easiest route, helping balance accessibility with opportunities for scientific discovery. It includes a current map, as well as the predicted map based on pattern recognition to predict future hazards. 

Ultimately, Astral Atlas demonstrates how NASA’s existing knowledge could be used not only to understand where exploration has already taken place, but also to guide where humanity should explore next.
details: It works as an interactive map, where you initially choose your objective, the start points, the crew limits and what you want to include on the map. The interface then shows all the hazards, predicted science, the explored and non explored areas, as well as the route to guide the astronaut. It has many benefits as it allows the astronaut to have a safe route to the expected destination and has exact timestamps of when the astronaut will reach each checkpoint. It has a dedicated section for safety, which means that the safety of the astronaut is always considered in the route chosen. The map can then be updated with new data from other sections of the Mars’ surface. We used JavaScript, Python, Claude, HTML, CSS as our main tools and software to create the website. Our project is creative as it not only includes the route, but all potential factors that might influence their route, like mentioned before.
